key_insight: NH4SCN promotes high-n quasi-2D scaffolds that template highly (110)-ordered 3D MAPbI3, rather than primarily improving charge transport through vertical 2D layers.
engineering_relevance: Controlling crystallization kinetics and lattice matching offers a route to better-ordered perovskite absorber films for solar cells.
method: Use NH4SCN to extend the nucleation window, suppressing n = 1 phases and promoting high-n scaffolds.
Probe phase formation and structural ordering using spectroscopy and structural analysis.
Examine cation-dependent lattice matching between quasi-2D scaffolds and 3D perovskite.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3 and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, supporting the proposed templating mechanism without reporting numerical device-performance gains.
watch_item: The effect is cation dependent and requires both compatible lattice spacing and successful kinetic control, limiting direct transfer to other formulations.
paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
